requirements.text: CodeWiki user slash command surface must be six commands: `/wiki bootstrap`, `/wiki status`, `/wiki resume`, `/wiki config`, `/wiki system <diagram type>`, and `/wiki product`. Bootstrap/config command adapters call backend functions directly instead of requiring dedicated normal agent tools.

Normal internal agent tool surface must be six tools: `wiki_state`, `wiki_decide`, `wiki_plan`, `wiki_implement`, `wiki_gate`, and `wiki_runtime`; low-level current tools become internal primitives or compatibility aliases.
`wiki_state` must support focused `view`/`lens` queries for graph subsets such as status, resume, trace, system, product, task, sprint, validation, runtime, and automation-readiness.
`lexicon.md` must be canonical, enforceable, pruned to active first-class terms, and free of unused glossary clutter.

Quality vocabulary must be gateway → gates → linters/tests → validation; tests remain executable code behavior only; audit/proof/check terminology is not canonical and remains only as migration/internal compatibility until removed.

Task done and sprint done must mean production-ready for their scopes; code-changing task closure requires passing code tests, required linters, gateway acceptance, task-close validation, and task-scoped ship-ready validation.

Automation readiness must be a graph/runtime contract for safe scheduling, blocking, retrying, or promotion using task boundary, accepted refs, gate policy, risk state, leases/worktrees, candidate files, model policy, blockers, context boundary, and deterministic next action.

accepted_decisions.summary: Public user commands are `/wiki bootstrap`, `/wiki status`, `/wiki resume`, `/wiki config`, `/wiki system <diagram type>`, and `/wiki product`.
Normal internal agent tools are `wiki_state`, `wiki_decide`, `wiki_plan`, `wiki_implement`, `wiki_gate`, and `wiki_runtime`.
`wiki_state` is the focused state/graph lens read API.
`lexicon.md` is canonical, enforceable, and pruned to active terms.
Quality vocabulary is gateway/gate/linter/test/validation; audit/proof/checks are migration/internal only.
Task done and sprint done mean production-ready for scope; ship-ready validates exact content candidate quality, while publication/release remain separate approval actions.
Automation readiness is a graph/runtime scheduling contract.
